pages.text: Thermia makes temperature matter. Everything around you pushes your body heat up or down: the sun, the wind, how wet you are, what you're standing next to. Get too hot or too cold and things go bad fast.

Configured entites have a $(l)natural temperature range$(). Step outside this range, and you'll begin experiencing the debilitating effects of $(l:tfc:thermia/heat)hyperthermia (overheating)$() or $(l:tfc:thermia/cold)hypothermia (freezing)$().$(br2)Your environment constantly influences your body temperature through factors like $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#solar_radiation)solar radiation$(), $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wind)wind$(), $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#humidity)humidity$(), $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wetness)wetness$(), nearby blocks, $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#insulation)and even your inventory$().

Thermia adds indicators to your HUD that display critical thermal information at a glance. Understanding these indicators is essential for survival.$(br2)The following pages will show you what each element means and how to read them effectively.
pages.title: Thermia GUI

pages.text: The Thermia GUI showing mild temperature conditions in the sun with a light breeze

The two thermometer icons show:$(br)$(li)Left: Your internal body temperature$(br)$(li)Right: Perceived Temperature$(br2)Colors shift from $(l)blue (cold)$() through white (comfortable) to $(l)red (hot)$(), giving you instant feedback on thermal conditions.
pages.title: Temperature Indicators

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Sun Icon:$() Brighter means more heating from sunlight$(li)$(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wind)$(l)Wind Arrow$():$() Wind speed and direction - points to the direction wind is moving$(li)$(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wetness)$(l)Water Droplet$():$() Your wetness level - affects cooling and insulation$(br2)These work together to determine your effective temperature.
